free_tier.stated: The free tier still exists and the pricing page still prints 'Free of charge' against input, output and caching for Gemini 3.8 Flash, 2.5 Flash-Lite and a dozen older models, but Google has stopped publishing how much the free tier carries. The rate-limits page now says only 'Rate limits depend on a variety of factors (such as your usage tier) and can be viewed in Google AI Studio', and the per-model free table the page carried through 2025 has been removed. The free columns that remain describe what is free, never how much. A Google AI Developers Forum post dated 2026-09-03 quotes 20 RPD on Gemini 3.8 Flash against 500 RPD on Flash-Lite.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: the free allowance is not the reason to use it: the Batch API at 100 concurrent requests and a 2GB input file is a paid-tier feature and the free-tier Batch rows read 'Not available', so a real batch needs the billing account the free tier exists to avoid.

limits.value: requests per day binds, not tokens: at a reported 20 RPD on Gemini 3.8 Flash the monthly ceiling is 600 requests, so a 1,000-item job at three requests an item never completes on one free project.

notes: Arithmetic, labelled estimate: 20 RPD x 30 days = 600 requests a month per model. The gap is the finding: a reader who trusts the word 'generous' on the pricing page and not the forum will design a batch that cannot run. Not measured: limits appear only in AI Studio after an account exists, so the 20 RPD figure rests on a forum report, and the 2025 archive's 250 RPD for 2.5 Flash disagrees with it by an order of magnitude. The corpus already carries google-gemini-api as qualifies-with-caveat on request-rate; this record adds the capacity shape and the fact that the number is no longer public.
